question: Is the full three-stage pipeline (context-enriched fine-tuning + iterative repair + RL) reproducible within plausible compute, and which stages must be off-the-shelf?
description: The full pipeline requires (i) building context subgraphs, (ii) an iterative repair loop with generated corrective examples, and (iii) an RL stage over a fine-tuned LM, with each stage re-trained and re-evaluated. If the RL stage alone is not reproducible on modest hardware, the investigation should be re-scoped to the supervised two-regime comparison plus a single-step repair, and H2 dropped or replaced by an offline replay/analysis.
rationale: RL fine-tuning of a 7B LM typically needs multi-GPU resources and stable reward plumbing; the plan currently assumes all three stages are runnable, which may be the binding constraint rather than the scientific question.
